scope: Bounded acquisition, local eligibility, search architecture, buyer-intent and reporting checks for an online-only Wonder and Method launch in Erie County NY.

interpretation.score_scale: 1-5 operating judgment: 1=poor fit or slow/uncertain, 5=strong fit or relatively fast/low-cost. Scores are not demand, rank, conversion or revenue probabilities.

interpretation.keyword_policy: Preserve all 482 inventory rows. Route synonyms and municipality modifiers to one appropriate canonical URL; do not create new pages solely for phrase coverage.

findings.issue: Online-only operations create an eligibility dead end for Google Business Profile.
findings.evidence: Google's current eligibility page requires in-person customer contact and lists online-only businesses, P.O. boxes and remote mailboxes as ineligible. The founder confirmed online-only launch operations.
findings.impact: Profile creation, virtual-office workarounds and Maps lead assumptions could cause suspension or fictitious pipeline.
findings.fix: Remove GBP/Maps from current acquisition and offer language; state online delivery plainly; reassess only after a real operating-model change.

findings.issue: A new domain has insufficient paid-client proof for premium outcome language.
findings.evidence: No Wonder and Method paid-client cases were supplied; Google people-first guidance favors first-hand experience and useful original content.
findings.impact: A concept or owned-site result could be read as a client outcome and weaken trust.
findings.fix: Label owned work, demo work and client work separately; disclose role, property, period, constraints and permissions; publish one inspectable sample artifact before broad content.

findings.issue: The 482-row inventory can trigger URL multiplication and intent cannibalization.
findings.evidence: V3 maps hundreds of design and SEO variants to two service URLs; Google warns against doorway and scaled low-value pages and recommends consistent canonical signals.
findings.impact: Thin town pages and duplicate service routes dilute maintenance, confuse buyers and create policy risk.
findings.fix: Preserve every row in the manifest but route by buyer job; use one county logistics page and gate any later page on distinct evidence.
findings.owner_or_gate: Root route manifest and editorial gate

findings.issue: Organic search alone is too slow and uncertain to carry early acquisition.
findings.evidence: Google states changes may take hours to several months and offers no indexing or ranking guarantee; third-party US keyword estimates are not Erie County demand.
findings.impact: A quiet first month could cause overproduction or cash stress while qualified buyers remain uncontacted.
findings.fix: Run technical SEO, proof content and a small authorized warm/partner lane in parallel; judge by qualified conversations, proposals, wins, cash and hours, not rank promises.

findings.issue: Directory and chamber profiles have asymmetric value and cost.
findings.evidence: Clutch Basic is free but has limited case studies, no verification and no website link from directory pages; BNP Pro Free advertises no charge and eligibility gates, while the V3 evidence observed a $50 application fee and the current general BNP application lists paid tiers at $1,750/$3,000 plus $30.
findings.impact: Automatic membership or paid verification could consume unknown startup cash without a qualified buyer path.
findings.fix: Use $0 profiles only after truthful proof exists; verify BNP terms; hold paid memberships until a named cohort, attendance plan and stop rule justify them.

findings.issue: Free advisory organizations are easy to mistake for referral channels.
findings.evidence: Buffalo State SBDC offers no-charge direct counseling to existing and prospective small businesses in Erie County/Niagara Frontier; SCORE offers free confidential mentoring to U.S.-based businesses, including remote sessions.
findings.impact: Time spent attending can be misclassified as pipeline, and pitching a resource community can damage fit.
findings.fix: Use SBDC/SCORE for offer, cash and buyer-question validation; log any introduction separately and do not forecast leads.

findings.issue: Search Console data cannot replace lead attribution.
findings.evidence: Google describes impressions, clicks, CTR and query/page dimensions; anonymized queries and aggregation mean exported rows do not represent every search or a causal lead path.
findings.impact: Visibility could be reported as qualified demand or revenue contribution.
findings.fix: Maintain a separate source-confidence lead log and review it with indexed canonical URLs and query/page data at days 7, 30, 60 and 90.

findings.issue: The post-launch content backlog can become a production quota.
findings.evidence: V3 contains twelve briefs and a stretch plan; Google warns that many pages generated primarily for search, including AI-generated pages without added value, can be scaled content abuse.
findings.impact: Founder hours move away from client delivery, proof and commercial page clarity.
findings.fix: Default to one fact-based asset in days 31-60 and one in days 61-90; require two observed 3-4h assets before any stretch run.

findings.issue: Paid or reciprocal local links would turn legitimate relationships into a ranking tactic.
findings.evidence: Google's spam policy identifies buying links, exchanging goods/services for links and excessive link exchanges as link spam.
findings.impact: Wasted spend, policy exposure and damaged partner trust.
findings.fix: Ask for no ranking link; collaborate only where the relationship has a real business or community purpose, with any commercial link qualified as required.
